message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season, which typically occurs from late winter to early spring. Male lions form coalitions and compete for dominance; the alpha male mates with females in his pride. Females are receptive for only a few days each year, during which they may mate with multiple males. Mating involves a brief copulation lasting a few minutes, after which the female may become pregnant. The male’s role is mainly to protect the pride and ensure his genes are passed on.
